messages:
mike_support: FYI NimbusAI is hitting big p95/p99 jumps and intermittent 429s on their dedicated eu-west-1 pool. Started ~1h ago after a burst. Customer reports steady error spikes and tail latency up to ~1.2s. Suspect noisy-neighbor / MIG contention on a shared host. alloc id: alloc-9a3f, node: gpu-node-14. Attaching trace + sample logs.

tony_sre: Can you paste the full alloc id, pod names and the node GPU ids? Also need nvidia-smi output and recent dmesg from the node. Any autoscale events around the time? :eyes:

mike_support: alloc-9a3f, pod=nimbus-prod-rl-7, podIP=10.12.8.34, node=gpu-node-14. autoscale-bot shows a scale-down ~45m ago then a scale-up ~10m ago.

autoscale-bot: [autoscale] scale-down triggered for pool eu-west-1-dedicated at 2026-03-15T12:18Z (reason: low throughput). scale-up triggered 2026-03-15T13:12Z (added 2 MIG slots).

elaine_enginfra: Paste `nvidia-smi -q` output and run `kubectl exec -it nimbus-prod-rl-7 -- dmesg | grep -i nvidia`. Also `cat /proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/*/information` — looking for clock throttle or ECC errors. If you can, grab `nv-hostengine` logs.

mike_support: Minimal nvidia-smi snippet from gpu-node-14 attached:
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 525.60.11    Driver Version: 525.60.11                         |
| GPU 0: A100-SXM4-40GB    MIG: 3g.20gb   99% GPU Utilization  MEM 95%        |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU 1: A100-SXM4-40GB    MIG: 7g.40gb   20% GPU Utilization  MEM 25%        |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
Also saw repeated `nvlink timeout` / `nv_peer_sm_teardown` messages in dmesg.

tony_sre: That pattern smells like asymmetric packing: a very heavy 3g slice on the same physical GPU with many smaller slices can push SM/warp scheduling to saturation. The NVSMI shows GPU0 pegged, GPU1 idle. Check MIG placement table: `redwoodctl pool describe eu-west-1-dedicated --node gpu-node-14` and `redwoodctl allocations list --node gpu-node-14`.

mike_support: Repro plan for customer: ramp Nimbus traffic to 120 rps targeting their 3g slice and monitor tail latency and 429 rate. Command we'll use locally:
```
wrk -t8 -c200 -d60s https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>"
```
Also capturing perf counters: sm__throughput.avg, l2_read_hit, l2_read_miss.

elaine_enginfra: For immediate mitigation: either isolate Nimbus to its own physical host (remove co-tenants) or re-pack MIG slices so large slices don't co-reside with many small ones. Ops can run `redwoodctl mig-repack --node gpu-node-14 --goal isolate-tenant=nimbus-prod` during a maintenance window. Warning: repack may cause evictions and transient latency spikes.

sara_platform: Noted — if we evict and re-reserve capacity there will be short-term billing changes for reserved time. I'll prepare a customer-facing blurb explaining: cause (interference), mitigation steps, ETA for repack, and temporary rate-limit suggestions. Recommend offering a temporary quota increase or grace credits if they hit throttles.

mike_support: I'll run the repro and attach perf counters and flamegraph. Will also run `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` during the load. Tagging @elaine_enginfra and @tony_sre to coordinate repack windows. :thumbsup:
